historical_record.description: Built as the 19-storey Spreckels/Call Building at 'newspaper angle', the cluster of early skyscrapers around Market and 3rd streets. Gutted by fire in 1906 and rehabilitated.

Remodelled by architect Albert Roller as the Streamline Moderne Central Tower, in preparation for the 1939–1940 Golden Gate International Exposition and its 'Shine for '39' campaign. Storeys were added, but removing the dome brought the height down from 315 feet to 298 feet.
Recorded in the city's 2008 survey of the Transit Center District, adopted in 2012, as an individually significant building.
Refaced in concrete to designs by the architect Albert Roller, the dome removed for a six-story vertical addition and the whole given stripped-down Moderne detail.
Designed by the Reid Brothers in a florid Venetian Renaissance manner.
The Spreckels Building of 1896 was remodelled in 1938 by the Reid Brothers with Albert F. Roller. It is rated Category III under Article 11 of the Planning Code.

building.completed_conflict: The 2008 survey of this district dates the building to 1898; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1908. The report gives this building's date as 1896 in one passage and 1898 in another, and its post-earthquake rebuilding as 1907 in the narrative and 1908 in the inventory table.
